DESIGN-ONLY task (task #22) in /workspace/SuperGrok1.5. CPU-only: do NOT edit any repo file, do NOT build, do NOT run GPU work (a kernel builder owns the GPU+build right now). Your sole output = write /workspace/.parallelism_design.md (a NEW file outside the repo) and return a summary.

GOAL: design the metaprogrammed parallelism layer ("4D+ZeRO-3", owner-locked) over the SuperGrok L3-TC persistent megakernel, so Phase 2 (8xH100, owner provisions later) starts from a finished design and the rental window stays short. The owner's locked decisions (read /workspace/.campaign_plan.md, especially the "PARALLELISM DECISION — FINAL" and "#14 FINDING/FIT-CEILING" sections): 4D (DP×TP×PP; SP was judged moot at seq 4-17 but the template should keep the axis expressible) + ZeRO-3 + max batch; megakernels stay single-GPU-usable (degenerate no-comm specialization); H100-only portability (NVSHMEM fair game); CUDA-graph-captured multi-GPU step; incremental build+measure discipline (DP+ZeRO-2 baseline -> ZeRO-3 -> PP -> TP, each must beat the prior at target scale).

FIRST read the actual kernel architecture (read-only): csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh (phase structure P0/P1 fwd+bwd/grid barriers/P2 dW/P3 optimizer; the launch path ~:1089-1118), csrc/fused/megakernel_common.cuh (GridBarrier), csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh (M-tiling, dW split-K G=4 pattern), grokking_optimizers/dispatch.py (fused_train_step entry, _FUSED_L3_REAL), and the workspace/state layout (how params/grads/opt-state are packed — look at the launcher bindings in csrc/bindings/). Ground every design choice in what's actually there.

THE DESIGN DOC must cover, concretely (file paths, template signatures, ABI sketches — not prose generalities):
1. The compile-time parallelism config: a template parameter pack / constexpr config struct (DPDegree, TPDegree, PPDegree, ZeROStage, plus an SPDegree axis kept expressible-but-1) and how it specializes: <1,1,1,Z0> == today's megakernel BIT-IDENTICAL (zero overhead, no comm code emitted) — this is the single-GPU guarantee.
2. The multi-GPU step decomposition: where the megakernel gets CUT at the existing optimizer grid-barrier seam -> [fwd+bwd megakernel] -> reduce-scatter(grads) -> [sharded optimizer kernel] -> all-gather(params); which of the 11 optimizers' state shards trivially (elementwise: adamw/lion/grokfast/...) vs which need care (muon NS orthogonalization is per-MATRIX not elementwise; SG2 meta-net + segmented sort is per-TENSOR; prodigy/grokadamw have GLOBAL reduction scalars that need an extra tiny all-reduce); the CUDA-graph capture boundary; bucket/overlap strategy (can the reduce-scatter overlap P2 dW?).
3. ZeRO stages on this kernel: ZeRO-2 (state+grad shard, params resident — fits the intact megakernel) vs ZeRO-3 (param shard -> per-layer all-gather — analyze the options honestly: (a) full pre-gather before launch [no memory win], (b) per-phase gather between barrier phases, (c) in-kernel NVSHMEM gather [frontier]; recommend the increment path).
4. PP: where the megakernel could cut into pipeline stages (per-layer-block boundaries already separated by grid barriers?), microbatch scheduling (1F1B?), and what it does to the fwd+bwd fusion; honest cost analysis at 4-17 seq / small layer counts vs ladder depths (24-48 layers).
5. TP via device-initiated NVSHMEM inside the wgmma loops: a sketch of where the all-reduce would land (post-attention + post-FFN row-parallel/col-parallel split a la Megatron), the determinism (A/A/A) implications (fixed-order reduce across ranks), and the fallback (host-NCCL TP with the kernel split per-block) if device-TP proves infeasible; this is the frontier-risk piece — scope it as the LAST increment with an explicit go/no-go gate.
6. NCCL/NVSHMEM bootstrap + the Python orchestration deltas (dispatch.py fused_train_step -> a rank-aware variant; torchrun vs custom launcher; how wiring_check/tail-gate/A-A-A gates extend to N ranks — cross-rank bit-determinism gate).
7. What is single-GPU-unit-testable NOW (so I can author+test code before the 8xH100 window): single-rank NCCL (loopback) correctness of the step decomposition, template-instantiation compile tests for all config points, the sharded-optimizer kernel vs the fused tail at DP=1, graph-capture of the decomposed step on 1 GPU.
8. The measurement plan + kill-gates for each increment (what number must improve to keep each dimension), tied to the instance-hour budget.

Be honest about risks and unknowns; mark every speculative claim as such. This doc is the Phase-2 contract. Write it to /workspace/.parallelism_design.md.

1	# SuperGrok1.5 H100 Megakernel Campaign — MASTER PLAN
2	
3	Autonomous overnight run, started 2026-06-11. Owner asleep; directive: "keep working until I'm back; build out all cells; do the optimization loop until convergence with roofline verification."
4	**This file is the single source of truth — re-read on every context reset.**
5	Companion files: `/workspace/.sam_spec.md` (SAM 2nd-pass impl spec), `/workspace/.cleanup.sh` (disk hygiene), memory `overnight-autonomous-run.md`, the task list (operational queue).
6	
7	## Objective
8	Every one of the 33 cells (11 optimizers x 3 models: decoder/vit/mamba) becomes a REAL L3-TC persistent wgmma megakernel (fwd+bwd+optimizer fused in one launch), then is roofline-optimized to its ceiling. Verification metric = **% of bf16 peak FLOPs (989 TF/s) on tuning/roofline.py**. Strip eager + L3-scalar paths from the PRODUCTION path once a cell is converted (keep a parity oracle test-only — never wired into production).
9	
10	## Hard rules (never violate)
11	- NO functionality suppression — fix components, never stub/clamp-hide to pass a gate.
12	- Parity mandatory: fused kernel matches canonical csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h AND eager, within tol (SG-family ~3e-5, fp32 storage; bf16~1e-3 masks bugs). Only GPU-vs-fp64/eager gates count (CPU mirrors miss races). If an optimization breaks parity, DEBUG to keep BOTH speed + correctness; abandon only if truly irreconcilable.
13	- Portability: optimizer/model files are portable H100 components; compile.py is arch-agnostic. Optimize the SHARED component headers (lifts every cell that composes them); never specialize per-cell in a way that breaks reuse.
14	- No CUDA graphs. One canonical math source per component (+ update check_math_single_source.py manifest if a header changes).
15	- wiring_check.py is the arbiter — a cell is "L3-TC" only when it shows path=L3-TC-megakernel(wgmma) AND passes the tail-gate parity.
16	
17	## Decisions (locked)
18	- Roofline benchmark scale: **d=2048** (owner named no number; my rec; adjustable 1024 cheaper / 4096 max — FLAG before heavy GPU burn). The grokking RACE stays toy scale (d=128) = the science; the d=2048 benchmark is a SEPARATE config from the SAME portable components (proves portability + gives a meaningful roofline). Rationale: at d=128 the kernel levers are physics-inert (GEMMs too small to feed tensor cores); roofline % only moves with bigger GEMMs.
19	- Roofline opt = LOOP UNTIL CONVERGENCE per cell: propose optimization -> incremental rebuild (sccache) -> measure roofline % (min-of-N, quiet GPU) -> KEEP if % improves beyond noise floor AND parity green / else REVERT -> repeat until K consecutive non-improving attempts = that cell's ceiling. Then next cell. Final CROSS-CELL sweep (shared-component wins lift multiple cells).
20	- Batch size: SWEEP empirically at the benchmark config, LOCK the saturation knee (NOT a guessed 16384).
21	- Execution: Opus agents do content-heavy edits/builds (resilient vs the Fable competing-model classifier); THIS Fable thread orchestrates + judges + commits. ONE builder at a time (single _ops.so). Agents commit verified-green batches (durable).
22	- Disk (30GB root / 47GB volume / 200GB RAM): build scratch (sccache, torch_ext, TMPDIR) -> /dev/shm (RAM); repo+commits on /workspace volume; run /workspace/.cleanup.sh every watchdog cycle. sccache SCCACHE_DIR=/dev/shm/sccache 20G.
23	
24	## Cell inventory & status (live truth = wiring_check; 14/33 clean at start)
25	decoder: adamw OK | lion OK | grokfast OK | grokadamw OK | muon OK | prodigy NaN(fixing) | neuralgrok eager(rescope) | sg11 eager(SAM) | sg15 eager(SAM) | looksam eager(SAM) | sg2 eager(hardest)
26	vit:     adamw OK | lion OK | grokfast OK | grokadamw OK | muon OK | prodigy NaN(fixing) | neuralgrok eager | sg11 eager(SAM) | sg15 eager(SAM) | looksam eager(SAM) | sg2 eager
27	mamba:   adamw OK | lion OK | grokfast OK | grokadamw OK | prodigy NaN(fixing) | muon eager(port) | neuralgrok eager | sg11 eager(SAM,DORMANT) | sg15 eager(SAM,DORMANT) | looksam eager(SAM,DORMANT) | sg2 eager
28	Mamba SAM-family lands DORMANT: re-running mamba fwd twice risks the A/A/A determinism race (like mamba×prodigy) -> code-present but gated OUT of _L3_WGMMA_CELLS until A/A/A confirmed.
29	Won't-grok caveats (build kernels anyway, document honestly): SG11/SG15 memorize-then-collapse (meta-net dynamics, not kernel bug); SG2 won't grok until the CSA/HCA lightning-indexer fidelity gap is fixed (separate); neuralgrok L3 needs a double-compute rescope (eager seed fwd/bwd for the host amplifier).
30	
31	## Stages (ordered)
32	0. PREREQS [in progress]: sccache->RAM done; fix prodigy x3 NaN [building]; compile.py incremental verified.
33	1. COMPILE/DISPATCH: ship tuned winners (coverage 0->33); add SG_TUNED_TILE_M/TILE_N/DW_SPLITK search dims + per-model JSON schema (the real roofline lever short of kernel redesign). [analysis done]
34	2. BUILD OUT ALL CELLS to L3-TC: commit in-flight (decoder/muon, mamba/prodigy) -> muon/mamba (proven vit/decoder port) -> SAM 2nd-pass mechanism (/workspace/.sam_spec.md) -> looksam/SG11/SG15 x3 -> neuralgrok x3 (rescope) -> SG2 x3 (in-kernel segmented sort + meta-net composition). Gate each, commit per batch.
35	3. MULTI-CTA TILING INFRA (scale-independent): lift the one-CTA-per-SM cap; expose tile/grid dims to the autotuner.
36	4. ROOFLINE OPT: build d=2048 benchmark config -> SWEEP batch, lock optimal B -> per-cell hill-climb LOOP UNTIL CONVERGENCE -> cross-cell sweep.
37	5. PRODUCTION CLEANUP: strip eager/scalar from production path (keep parity oracle test-only); sync README/HANDOFF honesty.
38	Overflow: repo/portfolio hardening. mi300x/tpu: owner-gated provisioning AFTER H100 is done (conserve billing) — signal the owner when ready.
39	
40	## OPEN BLOCKER (~08:05) — multi-session edit-war
41	2+ other long-running `claude` sessions (PIDs 13920/48866 up 2 days, 779863 ~3h) are editing these megakernel files, colliding on builds (peer agent observed 50+ parallel nvcc), and `git checkout`-reverting fixes — source/binary diverged repeatedly; likely also the cause of the server rate-limit that killed the prodigy agent's final report. PINGED owner to pause them / confirm sole-driver. **HOLD launching new builders** until resolved (building into the collision wastes GPU + gets reverted). Prodigy fix committed (73e7170) to survive reverts; current _ops (07:56) passes both gates.
42	
43	## BUILD FAST-PATH (critical, learned this run)
44	Use `python setup.py build_ext --inplace` (reuses build/temp/build.ninja, recompiles ONLY changed TUs — ~25-170s). DO NOT use `pip install -e .` (PEP-660 editable spins a fresh build-temp, recompiles ~54/56 TUs from scratch — slow). TC mega TUs are ~3-8min each (cicc+ptxas, CUTLASS wgmma x8 OptIds). Isolate `--build-temp` to avoid the peer-session build/temp collision.
45	
46	## CORRECTED SEQUENCE + MAX-PTX (owner additions)
47	Per-cell "maximally built out" = L3-TC + parity + DISTINCT-math (verified by the wiring audit) + **MAX-PTX maximal**: WGMMA/TMA collectives + 0 register spills + inlined fast-math PTX (rsqrt.approx / ex2.approx / fma.rn / redux.sync). VERIFY via profile_maximal.py; FIX any newly-converted cell (SAM 2nd-pass / meta-net mu / NS / segmented-sort) that spilled or fell back to scalar — not "maximal" until it passes.
48	After ALL 33 built: run a **BASELINE roofline test** (all cells, the pre-modification %-of-peak reference) BEFORE any hill-climb modifications. Then hill-climb-to-convergence at d=2048, re-measuring each candidate vs the baseline (keep only provable gains), then a final re-measure vs baseline to report the delta. Baseline-before-modifications is mandatory.
49	FUNCTIONALITY (owner): single-step parity gates are necessary-not-sufficient — also run the grokking RACE (multi-step training) on the converted cells (grok where expected; documented collapse for SG11/15/SG2; flag any hidden bug).
50	
51	## Loop discipline (every re-invocation)
52	1. Review the last agent's RAW gate evidence (numbers, not claims — docs have overstated before).
53	2. Commit if green (local, NO push), update task status.
54	3. Run /workspace/.cleanup.sh (disk).
55	4. Launch next builder (ONE at a time); keep read-only prep agents parallel as useful.
56	5. Re-arm watchdog 1200-1800s; keep THIS thread light (gate numbers, not deep kernel content) to dodge the classifier.
57	6. PushNotify owner ONLY on: blocked-needs-decision / 3rd idle tick / loop ending / major event (CI red, plan-changing result). NOT routine progress.
58	
59	## Morning report to assemble when owner returns
60	True X/33 L3-TC + parity-clean; what committed; honest notes on won't-grok cells; roofline numbers if Stage 4 reached; the d-scale still adjustable; any blockers.
61	
62	## INSTANCE-HOUR MINIMIZATION + ROOFLINE-PERFORMANCE MAXIMALITY (owner directives, 2026-06-12 — these SUPERSEDE the max-PTX-gate plan)
63	
64	### Billing model (CORRECTED): minimize INSTANCE / BILLABLE WALL-CLOCK uptime, NOT "GPU hours"
65	The instance bills by wall-clock uptime regardless of GPU util -> an IDLE instance still costs money (earlier "idle GPU is fine" framing was WRONG). Minimize TOTAL uptime to completion:
66	(a) Keep the GPU pipeline FULL with NECESSARY work — no idle gaps in the critical path; as one GPU job ends, the next necessary one starts.
67	(b) Overlap CPU-bound work (sccache compiles, disasm, edits) WITH GPU work so the critical path is shortest.
68	(c) Saturating the GPU to finish a NECESSARY job faster is GOOD (fewer billable hours).
69	(d) Do NOT manufacture UNNECESSARY work (also extends uptime).
70	(e) The exhaustive hill-climb IS necessary work — run it FULLY but EFFICIENTLY (cache + subset-race measurement + no idle).
71	(f) Async = orchestration never blocks; still ONE heavy GPU kernel at a time (two contend + OOM).
72	(g) TEAR-DOWN signal: tell owner the moment the campaign converges so they can kill the instance.
73	
74	### Maximality = ROOFLINE PERFORMANCE, not PTX/SASS (CORRECTED)
75	Owner: "I don't want PTX maximality, I want performance maximality based on the roofline test." The roofline % is the SOLE objective function. profile_maximal / PTX tricks (rsqrt.approx, ex2.approx, fma.rn, redux.sync, zero-spill, WGMMA/TMA) are DEMOTED from a GATE to a SOURCE OF CANDIDATE MOVES — proposed, tried, KEPT ONLY IF the roofline number improves. Old #17 (max-PTX as a gate) is DROPPED as a gate.
76	THE LOOP (exhaustive hill-climb to convergence): propose an optimization -> recompile (sccache, fast) -> measure roofline on the RACE (or a race subset) -> compare to previous best -> KEEP if roofline improves AND parity/functionality stays green / else REVERT -> repeat until nothing improves. Then next file.
77	SCOPE = ALL 15 portable files: the 3 model files (decoder/vit/mamba megakernels) + the 11 optimizer files + the compile/dispatch file.
78	PORTABILITY constraint (hard): these are portable to OTHER projects -> optimize the SHARED/portable components; never specialize per-cell in a way that breaks reuse.
79	GUARDRAIL: parity + race functionality must stay green for every KEPT optimization (roofline gain with broken correctness is rejected). The functional gauntlet (wiring smoke + tail-gate parity/A-A-A + the race outcomes + audit fixes #19) is the CORRECTNESS baseline the hill-climb must preserve — still required, just not as the maximality metric.
80	WORKLOAD: use the ACTUAL RACE (grokking_race_v2.py) or a SUBSET (few steps / 1 seed / representative cells) as the roofline timing workload. sccache for fast recompiles in the loop.
81	OPEN FORK (resolve BEFORE the hill-climb): roofline SCALE — toy d=128 actual race is physics-capped (GEMMs too small to feed tensor cores -> levers inert, % flat, hill-climb chases noise; real levers become occupancy/launch-overhead) VS a scaled d=2048 race (same portable code path, tensor-core/tiling/split-K levers actually move the %). Asked owner 2026-06-12.
82	
83	### tpu_v6e + mi300x: DO NOT provision yet. Signal owner the moment H100 is LOCKED (all 15 files roofline-converged + race/parity-verified). Provisioning early = idle accel-hours + porting a moving target. Components are arch-agnostic by design.
84	
85	## SCALING + MULTI-GPU + BATCH STRATEGY (developed 2026-06-12 — owner constraints + analysis SETTLED; the RECOMMENDATION is PROPOSED, awaiting owner confirm to lock + start #14). This RESOLVES the earlier "OPEN FORK d=128 vs d=2048": answer = scale the REAL models up a GPT-2/3 ladder.
86	
87	### Owner constraints (SETTLED)
88	- Goal = B: peak-performance PORTABLE megakernel artifact; metric = roofline %; scale the REAL models (not a synthetic config) so it's also non-toy SCIENCE.
89	- Not afraid of >1B params; wants size presets beyond "large" (xl/xxl/3xl/...).
90	- Willing up to 8xH100 multi-GPU, and WILL do the FULL NCCL/distributed-systems engineering.
91	- Distributed works on H100 (NCCL) + mi300x (RCCL); NOT tpu_v6e (single-device only).
92	- Batch size is a first-class axis.
93	
94	### Size ladder (COMPUTED params + 80GB-H100 memory facts; prime->251; GPT-2/3-anchored aspect ratios 33-80:1, all in published range)
95	MODEL_SCALES extension (drop-in). decoder~=vit; mamba~=half.
96	  xl  768/12/12  GPT2-small  dec~85M  | xxl 1024/24/16 GPT2-medium ~303M | 3xl 1280/36/20 GPT2-large ~709M
97	  4xl 1600/48/25 GPT2-XL ~1.48B | 5xl 2048/48/16 ~2.42B | 6xl 2560/32/20 GPT3-2.7B ~2.52B
98	  (7xl=GPT3-6.7B d4096; 8xl=GPT3-13B = multi-GPU/ZeRO ONLY.)
99	80GB WALL is OPTIMIZER-DEPENDENT (mem = optstate ∝ params + activations ∝ batch·d·layers):
100	  heavy-state (SG2 ~44B/param, SG11/15): fit to ~4xl/GPT2-XL (65GB); 5xl OOM single-GPU.
101	  lean (adamw ~18B/param): fit to ~6xl/2.5B single-GPU. mamba (half params): not memory-limited on this ladder.
102	
103	### Distributed RULE (technical truth, not a preference): WRAP the megakernel, never SPLIT it.
104	- DP + ZeRO-3 (shard optstate/weights): each GPU runs the FULL fwd+bwd+opt megakernel on a batch/state shard; NCCL collectives (reduce-scatter grad, all-gather weight) happen BETWEEN steps, AROUND the kernel -> megakernel stays one-per-step + portable. OK.
105	- Tensor/pipeline parallelism needs cross-GPU sync INSIDE fwd/bwd -> breaks the single-kernel design (the whole asset). DO NOT.
106	- ZeRO-3 alone reaches ~6.7B on 8x80GB; CAP there (past it: per-GPU % flat, science silly, hours balloon).
107	- Per-GPU roofline % saturates ~GPT2-XL; multi-GPU's NEW result = near-linear 1->8 SCALING EFFICIENCY (+ fits heavy cells bigger), NOT a higher %.
108	
109	### Accelerator portability mapping (matches owner's distributed constraint)
110	- H100: NCCL = flagship distributed platform.
111	- mi300x: RCCL (drop-in NCCL-equiv) + existing gfx942 megakernel path -> DP+ZeRO layer PORTS = "distributed on AMD" proof.
112	- tpu_v6e: single-device Pallas/XLA (no NCCL; owner won't build TPU-distributed) = "components port to a non-GPU accelerator" breadth proof, single-device.
113	
114	### Batch = per-tier SWEPT axis, NOT one locked number
115	- Batch = GEMM M-dim (M = batch·seq); at tiny seq (decoder=4) it's CO-EQUAL with d for roofline %. Per-(model,tier) SATURATION KNEE: below=tensor cores starve, above=wasted memory.
116	- Knee moves DOWN as d grows (big GEMMs saturate at smaller batch; d=128 needed ~16k + still occ-pinned 8x under = the #14 problem).
117	- Batch COMPETES with optstate for 80GB -> big-d heavy cells get batch-squeezed (caps %); ZeRO frees it back.
118	- COUPLES to grokking science (full- vs mini-batch on small datasets) -> saturation-knee batch for ROOFLINE, grok-appropriate batch for SCIENCE (2 configs).
119	- Multi-GPU = batch scaling: WEAK-SCALE (local batch=knee, global=8xknee) keeps per-GPU % high for the curve.
120	- Generalize #16 ("one batch @d2048") -> "knee per ladder tier"; fold batch into the hill-climb search (interacts w/ #12 tile dims).
121	
122	### RECOMMENDATION (PROPOSED — awaiting owner confirm; the ONE open dial = flagship top 2.7B vs 6.7B, my pick 6.7B)
123	- MODELS: all 3 for breadth. DECODER = flagship (cleanest GEMM, highest ceiling). VIT = transformer-portability twin. MAMBA = breadth proof w/ HONESTLY-LOWER ceiling (sequential scan; only proj GEMMs feed TC) — DON'T push mamba to the huge sizes.
124	- SIZES per claim: roofline-% showcase @ GPT2-XL/4xl (all 33 cells, 1/GPU, no ZeRO); distributed/scaling FLAGSHIP @ GPT3-6.7B/7xl (decoder+lean, DP+ZeRO 8xH100, report 1->8 near-linear); SCIENCE grok-demo @ GPT2-medium/xxl (303M, meaningful+cheap); full roofline CURVE xl->4xl(->6xl/7xl lean).

120	// Rebase a FusedOptState's per-element state pointers to a parameter-tensor
121	// slice at `off` within the flat [m|v|extra] layout. Per-TENSOR fields (the
122	// NeuralGrok psi MLP weights) and all scalars pass through unchanged.
123	template <OptId Opt>
124	__device__ __forceinline__ FusedOptState
125	rebase_state(const FusedOptState& s, int64_t off) {
126	    FusedOptState t = s;  // scalars + per-tensor pointers copy as-is
127	    if (t.exp_avg)    t.exp_avg    += off;
128	    if (t.exp_avg_sq) t.exp_avg_sq += off;
129	    if (t.ema)        t.ema        += off;
130	    if (t.sam_dir)    t.sam_dir    += off;
131	    if (t.s_track)    t.s_track    += off;
132	    if (t.mu)         t.mu         += off;
133	    if (t.orth)       t.orth       += off;
134	    if (t.smart_grad) t.smart_grad += off;
135	    if (t.param_init) t.param_init += off;   // Prodigy trajectory anchor p0
136	    if (t.sharpness)  t.sharpness  += off;   // SuperGrok11/15 (g_sam−g)² (per element)
137	    // SuperGrok11/15 phi weights (sg_phi_W1/b1/W2) are a per-TENSOR weight SET (same
138	    // for every element), NOT a per-element slice — so they are NOT rebased (the same
139	    // pointer is staged to SMEM once per block, exactly like NeuralGrok's psi pointers).
140	    return t;
141	}

154	    const int* tokens;   // [B, kSeq] int32 token ids in [0, kVocab)

156	    int        B;        // batch size (full-batch in the race ≈ 4191)

172	                         float* __restrict__ params,
173	                         DecoderTokenCtx tok,
174	                         float* __restrict__ grad,        // reduced grad [total]
175	                         float lr, int step, FusedOptState st) {

254	        TaskQueue q = ctx.queue();
255	        for (int t = q.next_block(&task_slot); t < kDecNumTensors;
256	             t = q.next_block(&task_slot)) {
257	            const int n = kDecSizes[t];
258	            const int64_t off = (int64_t)kDecOffsets[t];
259	            const FusedOptState ts = rebase_state<Opt>(st, off);
260	            float* __restrict__ p = params + off;
261	            const float* __restrict__ gg = grad + off;
262	            for (int i = threadIdx.x; i < n; i += blockDim.x)
263	                apply_optimizer<Opt>(p, gg, (int64_t)i, step, ts);
264	        }
265	    }
266	}

268	// ── Host launcher — one persistent CTA per SM, 256 threads/CTA (2 warp-groups).
269	//    Mirrors launch_fused_megakernel's hang-freedom contract: occupancy≥1 or
270	//    refuse (the GridBarrier rendezvous of n_ctas CTAs can never complete if a
271	//    CTA can't be placed). Zeroes the barrier+task counters per launch. ─────────
272	template <OptId Opt>
273	cudaError_t launch_fused_decoder_megakernel(
274	        PersistentContext ctx, float* params, DecoderTokenCtx tok,
275	        float* grad, float lr, int step, FusedOptState st, cudaStream_t stream) {
276	    int dev = 0;
277	    cudaError_t err = cudaGetDevice(&dev);
278	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
279	    int n_sms = 0;
280	    err = cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&n_sms, cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount, dev);
281	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
282	
283	    int occ = 0;
284	    err = cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor(
285	        &occ, (const void*)&fused_decoder_megakernel<Opt>, SG_TUNED_MEGA_BLOCK,
286	        /*dynamicSMemBytes=*/0);
287	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
288	    // Hang-freedom: at least one CTA per SM must be resident or the grid barrier
289	    // can never be satisfied. The L3-REAL kernel uses ≈42 KB static smem + a high
290	    // register count; if it cannot place one block/SM, REFUSE rather than hang.
291	    assert(occ >= 1 &&
292	           "fused_decoder_megakernel: 0 blocks/SM — GridBarrier would hang. The "
293	           "decoder smem (~42KB) + regs exceed one-block-per-SM occupancy; "
294	           "reduce footprint or fall back to the L1 per-op path.");
295	    if (occ < 1) return cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources;
296	
297	    const unsigned launch_ctas = (unsigned)n_sms;
298	    ctx.n_ctas = launch_ctas;
299	
300	    if (ctx.g_arrived) { err = cudaMemsetAsync(ctx.g_arrived, 0, sizeof(unsigned), stream); if (err) return err; }
301	    if (ctx.g_generation) { err = cudaMemsetAsync(ctx.g_generation, 0, sizeof(unsigned), stream); if (err) return err; }
302	    if (ctx.g_next_task) { err = cudaMemsetAsync(ctx.g_next_task, 0, sizeof(int), stream); if (err) return err; }
303	
304	    dim3 grid(launch_ctas), block(SG_TUNED_MEGA_BLOCK);
305	    fused_decoder_megakernel<Opt><<<grid, block, 0, stream>>>(
306	        ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st);
307	    return cudaGetLastError();
308	}

310	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
311	//  WGMMA CELL DRIVER (DESIGN-TC-PIPELINE.md Fork B, R2.3). Compiled only under
312	//  the wgmma token; the scalar path above is untouched.
313	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
314	#if (SG_TUNED_GEMM_IMPL == SG_GEMM_IMPL_WGMMA)
315	
316	// TC megakernel threads: 256 (the engine's producer+consumer warpgroup layout;
317	// wgmma is warpgroup-scoped on threads 0..127). We do NOT apply the scalar
318	// path's asymmetric setmaxnreg (dealloc<32> on WG0) — that would STARVE the MMA
319	// warpgroup (WG0 issues the wgmma; a 128-wide accumulator needs 64 fp32 regs/
320	// thread). The validated selftest ran no split; we match it.
321	#define SG_TC_MEGA_BLOCK 256
322	
323	// ── smem arena for the unpipelined engine: one A(64×16) + one B(N×16) bf16 tile
324	//    + the 256-float reduction slot. 16B-aligned. N = SG_TUNED_TILE_N. The 9 dW
325	//    specs live here too (identical for all threads → shared, not per-thread
326	//    stack: keeps the launch's local-memory reservation small so the persistent
327	//    kernel places on a memory-tight GPU). ──
328	struct DecTcSmem {
329	    // kDecTcStages A(64×16) + kDecTcStages B(N×16) bf16 tiles — the GEMM K-loop
330	    // double-buffer ring (slot s at sA + s*64*16 / sB + s*N*16). At S=2 + N=128
331	    // the ring is 2·(2KB+4KB)=12KB; DecTcSmem total ~13.5KB ≪ the 48KB static cap.
332	    __nv_bfloat16 sA[dectc::kDecTcStages * 64 * 16];
333	    __nv_bfloat16 sB[dectc::kDecTcStages * SG_TUNED_TILE_N * 16];
334	    float red[256];
335	    dectc::DecDwSpec spec[9];
336	};
337	
338	// ── TC workspace layout (carved from tok.workspace; the host sizes it for the
339	//    TC path — see dec_tc_workspace_floats). Regions (float units):
340	//      [0 .. acts_f)                      : DecActs bf16 region (reinterpreted)
341	//      [acts_f .. acts_f + nCTA*scratch)  : per-CTA tile scratch (f32)
342	//      [.. + nCTA*kLnVecElems)            : per-CTA LN-vec partials (f32)
343	//      [.. + nCTA)                        : per-CTA loss slots (f32)
344	//      [.. + 1)                           : reduced scalar loss (host reads it)
345	//    acts_f = ceil(acts_bf16 / 2). ──
346	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t dec_tc_acts_floats(int T, int B) {
347	    // mirror dectc::dec_acts_bind's running offset (bf16 elems) → floats.
348	    const int64_t d = dec::kD, dff = dec::kDff, V = dec::kVocab, L = dec::kLayers;
349	    const int64_t Td = (int64_t)T * d, T3d = (int64_t)T * 3 * d, Tff = (int64_t)T * dff;
350	    int64_t bf = 0;
351	    for (int li = 0; li < L; ++li) bf += Td + Td + Td + Tff + T3d + Td + Tff + Td;
352	    bf += (int64_t)B * d + (int64_t)B * V + Td;     // X_hn + dY_logits + dh0
353	    return (bf + 1) / 2;
354	}
355	// dW split-K partial floats (0 when G==1 → no extra scratch, single-CTA path).
356	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t dec_tc_dw_part_floats() {
357	    return (dectc::kDecDwSplitK > 1) ? dectc::dec_dw_part_floats(dectc::kDecDwSplitK) : 0;
358	}
359	// STAGED-optimizer cross-CTA reduction scratch (Prodigy d-estimate). The Prodigy
360	// stage publishes per-CTA (r,s) slots (2*nCTA) + a reduced-d slot (1) — an owner-
361	// computes tree (opt_stages_precompute.cuh), NO float atomic. Sized for the
362	// LARGEST nCTA (one CTA/SM = #SMs); tiny (≤ 2*132+1 ≈ 1 KB) and carved
363	// UNCONDITIONALLY so the opt-agnostic host launcher (dec_tc_launcher_scratch)
364	// allocates one workspace that fits every OptId. Unused by AdamW/Lion/… (their
365	// P3 never touches this region), so adding it leaves those cells byte-identical.
366	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t dec_tc_opt_reduce_floats(int nCTA) {
367	    return (int64_t)2 * nCTA + 1;            // [r slots | s slots | reduced d]
368	}
369	// ── Muon (STAGED grid-cooperative Newton-Schulz) per-matrix scratch. IDENTICAL in
370	//    shape to the vit twin (vit_tc_muon_floats): the NS chain runs ONE 2D weight at
371	//    a time over all CTAs; the scratch holds X/A/AX/AAX/orth for the LARGEST 2D weight
372	//    + the per-CTA Frobenius-norm partials + inv_norm. The momentum buffer (muon_buf)
373	//    is NOT here — it PERSISTS across steps as optimizer state, bound to the m slice
374	//    (st.exp_avg). Largest decoder 2D weight: ff.0/ff.2 = 512×128 = 65536 numel; largest
375	//    rows = 512 ⇒ A = 512×512 (dectc::kDecMuonMaxNumel/kDecMuonMaxRows). Carved
376	//    UNCONDITIONALLY (≈ 4·65536 + 512² + nCTA + 1 floats ≈ 2 MB) so the opt-agnostic
377	//    launcher (dec_tc_launcher_scratch) fits every OptId; unused by every non-Muon cell
378	//    (its P2.7/P3-2D branches are if-constexpr'd out → byte-identical). ──
379	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t dec_tc_muon_floats(int nCTA) {
380	    // X + AX + AAX + orth (each maxNumel) + A (maxRows²) + nrm_partials(nCTA) + inv_norm(1)
381	    return (int64_t)4 * dectc::kDecMuonMaxNumel
382	         + (int64_t)dectc::kDecMuonMaxRows * dectc::kDecMuonMaxRows
383	         + nCTA + 1;
384	}
385	// ── LookSAM (STAGED in-kernel SAM 2nd backward) transient scratch. The SAM step
386	//    perturbs p in place, runs a SECOND fwd+bwd at p', and needs (a) a param BACKUP
387	//    for the exact restore (eager clones p before perturbing) + (b) a SEPARATE g_sam
388	//    grad buffer so the 2nd backward does NOT clobber the first grad `grad` (sam_dir
389	//    = g_sam − grad reads both). Both are total-sized + transient (NOT persistent
390	//    state — sam_dir itself persists in the `extra` state slice, bound by the cell).
391	//    Carved UNCONDITIONALLY (≈ 2·422755 ≈ 3.4 MB) so the opt-agnostic launcher fits
392	//    every OptId; unused by every non-LookSAM cell (its phase is if-constexpr'd out
393	//    → byte-identical). nrm_partials(nCTA)+inv_norm(1) for the ‖g‖ reduction reuse
394	//    the loss workspace (sq_part/coef_bc, as GrokAdamW's P2.5 does), so no extra here. ──
395	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t dec_tc_looksam_floats() {
396	    return (int64_t)2 * kDecTotalElems;       // [sam_backup | sam_grad]
397	}
398	// ── SuperGrok2 compile-time dims = the race config (== SG2Dims defaults). The
399	//    composed megakernel reads weights from HBM, so the only SG2 workspace is the
400	//    per-CTA meta-net scratch (sg2_ws_stride, sized for the LARGEST tensor — the
401	//    65536-element ff weights — which bounds every tensor's intermediates + the
402	//    in-kernel segmented-sort key/idx/perm/unsort). ──
403	using DecSG2Dims = SG2Dims<>;
404	constexpr int kDecSG2Nmax = 65536;   // max(kDecSizes) — the per-CTA carve upper bound
405	// Per-CTA SG2 slice = row_off64 staging (kDecNumTensors int64 = 2*N floats) + the
406	// meta-net scratch (sized for the largest tensor). The row_off64 prefix lets the
407	// SG2State.row_off (const int64_t*) be built on-device from the __constant__ int
408	// kDecOffsets (the adapter for the int-typed layout tables).
409	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t dec_sg2_ws_stride_floats() {
410	    return (int64_t)2 * kDecNumTensors
411	         + sg2_ws_stride<DecSG2Dims>((int64_t)kDecSG2Nmax);
412	}
413	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t dec_tc_sg2_floats(int nCTA) {
414	    // +1 for the 8-byte realignment slack of sg2_ws_base (the per-CTA slice fronts an
415	    // int64 row_off64 array; kDecTotalElems is odd, so the base may need a +1 bump).
416	    return (int64_t)nCTA * dec_sg2_ws_stride_floats() + 1;
417	}
418	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t dec_tc_workspace_floats(int T, int B, int nCTA) {
419	    return dec_tc_acts_floats(T, B)
420	         + (int64_t)nCTA * dectc::dec_tile_scratch_total_f32()
421	         + (int64_t)nCTA * dectc::kLnVecElems
422	         + nCTA + 1
423	         + dec_tc_dw_part_floats()            // split-K dW partials (G>1)
424	         + dec_tc_opt_reduce_floats(nCTA)     // STAGED-opt (Prodigy) reduce slots
425	         + dec_tc_muon_floats(nCTA)           // STAGED-opt (Muon) NS per-matrix scratch
426	         + dec_tc_looksam_floats()            // STAGED-opt (LookSAM) SAM 2nd-bwd scratch
427	         + dec_tc_sg2_floats(nCTA);           // SuperGrok2 meta-net per-CTA scratch (carve-LAST)
428	}

430	template <OptId Opt>
431	__global__ void __launch_bounds__(SG_TC_MEGA_BLOCK)
432	fused_decoder_megakernel_tc(PersistentContext ctx,
433	                            float* __restrict__ params,
434	                            DecoderTokenCtx tok,
435	                            float* __restrict__ grad,
436	                            float lr, int step, FusedOptState st) {
437	    __shared__ DecTcSmem sm;
438	    GridBarrier bar = ctx.barrier();
439	    const int cta = blockIdx.x;
440	    const int nCTA = (int)ctx.n_ctas;
441	    const int B = tok.B;
442	    const int T = B * dec::kSeq;
443	
444	    // Workspace partition.
445	    float* ws = tok.workspace;
446	    const int64_t acts_f = dec_tc_acts_floats(T, B);
447	    __nv_bfloat16* acts_base = reinterpret_cast<__nv_bfloat16*>(ws);
448	    float* scratch_base = ws + acts_f;
449	    const int64_t scratch_per = dectc::dec_tile_scratch_total_f32();
450	    float* lnvec_base = scratch_base + (int64_t)nCTA * scratch_per;
451	    float* loss_part  = lnvec_base + (int64_t)nCTA * dectc::kLnVecElems;
452	    float* loss_out   = loss_part + nCTA;
453	    // Split-K dW partials (G>1): the (gt,kc) 64×N partial tiles, carved AFTER the
454	    // loss slot (matches dec_tc_workspace_floats's term order). G==1 → dw_part unused.
455	    float* dw_part    = loss_out + 1;
456	    const int kDwG    = dectc::kDecDwSplitK;
457	    // STAGED-opt cross-CTA reduce slots (Prodigy d), carved AFTER the dW partials
458	    // (matches dec_tc_workspace_floats's term order). Unused unless Opt==Prodigy.
459	    float* opt_reduce = dw_part + dec_tc_dw_part_floats();
460	    // Muon NS per-matrix scratch, carved AFTER the Prodigy reduce slots (matches
461	    // dec_tc_workspace_floats's term order — carving it LAST keeps every prior
462	    // region's offset unchanged, so the 5 already-green cells are byte-identical).
463	    // Unused unless Opt==Muon. Layout (mirrors the vit twin):
464	    //   [muon_X | muon_AX | muon_AAX | muon_orth] (each kDecMuonMaxNumel)
465	    //   [muon_A (kDecMuonMaxRows²)] [nrm_partials (nCTA)] [inv_norm (1)]
466	    float* muon_base = opt_reduce + dec_tc_opt_reduce_floats(nCTA);
467	    // LookSAM SAM 2nd-backward scratch, carved AFTER the Muon scratch (term order
468	    // matches dec_tc_workspace_floats — carving it LAST keeps every prior region's
469	    // offset unchanged, so the already-green cells are byte-identical). Layout:
470	    //   [sam_backup (total)] [sam_grad (total)]. Unused unless Opt==LookSAM.
471	    float* sam_backup = muon_base + dec_tc_muon_floats(nCTA);
472	    float* sam_grad   = sam_backup + kDecTotalElems;
473	    // SuperGrok2 meta-net per-CTA scratch, carved AFTER the LookSAM sam_grad (term
474	    // order matches dec_tc_workspace_floats — carving it LAST keeps every prior
475	    // region's offset unchanged, so the already-green cells are byte-identical).
476	    // Each CTA owns dec_sg2_ws_stride_floats() (row_off64 staging + meta-net scratch).
477	    // ALIGN to 8 bytes (even float offset): the per-CTA slice fronts an int64
478	    // row_off64 staging array; kDecTotalElems is odd so sam_grad+total lands on an
479	    // odd float offset (4-byte) → an int64 read there is a misaligned address. Round
480	    // up to the next even float. The carve term dec_tc_sg2_floats reserves the stride
481	    // per CTA; the +1 alignment slack fits within the acts/scratch headroom (the
482	    // workspace is over-sized) and dec_sg2_ws_stride_floats() is even, so every CTA
483	    // base stays 8-byte aligned. Unused unless Opt==SuperGrok2.
484	    float* sg2_ws_base = sam_grad + kDecTotalElems;
485	    if (((uintptr_t)sg2_ws_base & 0x7) != 0) sg2_ws_base += 1;   // → 8-byte aligned
486	    (void)sg2_ws_base;   // referenced only by the SuperGrok2 P3-SG2 phase
487	
488	    dectc::DecActs acts = dectc::dec_acts_bind(acts_base, T, B);
489	    dectc::DecTileScratch sc = dectc::dec_tile_scratch_bind(scratch_base + (int64_t)cta * scratch_per);
490	    float* my_lnvec = lnvec_base + (int64_t)cta * dectc::kLnVecElems;
491	
492	    DecWeights w = dec_bind(params);
493	
494	    // ── P0: zero this CTA's LN-vec partials + loss slot (dW/embed grads are
495	    //    written-once → no pre-zero). ──
496	    for (int i = threadIdx.x; i < dectc::kLnVecElems; i += blockDim.x) my_lnvec[i] = 0.0f;
497	    if (threadIdx.x == 0) loss_part[cta] = 0.0f;
498	    bar.sync();   // B0
499	
500	    // ── P1: token-tile-parallel fwd+bwd. Each CTA grid-strides over tiles of
501	    //    kTileM rows; for its tile it runs fwd (→ acts X, NLL) then bwd (→ acts
502	    //    dY, dh0, LN-vec partials). Barrier-free within the tile. ──
503	    const int nrows_tile = dectc::kTileM;
504	    const int n_tiles = (T + nrows_tile - 1) / nrows_tile;
505	    float nll_acc = 0.0f;
506	    for (int ti = cta; ti < n_tiles; ti += nCTA) {
507	        const int g0 = ti * nrows_tile;
508	        const int nrows = (T - g0) < nrows_tile ? (T - g0) : nrows_tile;
509	        float nll = dectc::dectc_forward_tile(w, g0, nrows, acts, sc, tok.tokens, tok.targets,
510	                                              sm.sA, sm.sB, sm.red);
511	        dectc::dectc_backward_tile(w, g0, nrows, B, acts, sc, tok.targets,
512	                                   my_lnvec, sc.work2, sm.sA, sm.sB, sm.red);
513	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) nll_acc += nll;
514	        __syncthreads();
515	    }
516	    if (threadIdx.x == 0) loss_part[cta] = nll_acc;
517	    bar.sync();   // B1: all acts (X + dY) + LN-vec partials complete
518	
519	    // ── P2: assemble all 30 grads into `grad`. dW output-stationary (gt %
520	    //    nCTA), biases, embedding owner-scan, LN-vec reduce. No partials. The 9
521	    //    dW specs are built into SHARED smem (thread 0; identical for all) so the
522	    //    9-spec array is NOT on every thread's stack (shrinks the launch's local
523	    //    reservation — the persistent kernel must place on a memory-tight GPU). ──
524	    if (threadIdx.x == 0) dectc::dectc_build_dw_specs(acts, B, T, sm.spec);
525	    __syncthreads();
526	    dectc::DecDwSpec* spec = sm.spec;
527	    const int n_dw = dectc::dectc_dw_total_tiles<SG_TUNED_TILE_N>(spec);
528	    if (kDwG > 1) {
529	        // SPLIT-K (multi-CTA tiling): fan (n_dw·G) (tile,chunk) partials over the
530	        // grid so the ~62% idle SMs do work; deterministic ascending-chunk reduce.
531	        for (int item = cta; item < n_dw * kDwG; item += nCTA) {
532	            const int gt = item / kDwG, kc = item % kDwG;
533	            dectc::dectc_dw_run_tile_splitk<SG_TUNED_TILE_N>(spec, gt, kc, kDwG, dw_part, sm.sA, sm.sB);
534	        }
535	        bar.sync();   // all (gt,kc) partials complete before the reduce reads them
536	        dectc::dectc_dw_reduce_splitk<SG_TUNED_TILE_N>(spec, n_dw, kDwG, dw_part, grad, cta, nCTA);
537	    } else {
538	        for (int gt = cta; gt < n_dw; gt += nCTA)
539	            dectc::dectc_dw_run_tile<SG_TUNED_TILE_N>(spec, gt, grad, sm.sA, sm.sB);
540	    }
541	    dectc::dectc_dw_biases(spec, grad);
542	    dectc::dectc_embed_owner_scan(acts, tok.tokens, T, grad, cta, nCTA);
543	    dectc::dectc_lnvec_reduce(lnvec_base, grad, nCTA, cta);
544	    // Loss reduce (fp64) by CTA 0.
545	    if (cta == 0 && threadIdx.x == 0) {
546	        double s = 0.0;
547	        for (int c = 0; c < nCTA; ++c) s += (double)loss_part[c];
548	        *tok.loss_out = (float)(s / (double)B);
549	    }
550	    (void)loss_out;
551	    bar.sync_reset(ctx.g_next_task);   // B2: reduced grad ready; reset queue
552	
553	    // ── P2.4 (LookSAM ONLY, SAM steps): the MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd backward that
554	    //    produces st.sam_dir = g_sam − g (INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES §6). Eager LookSAM,
555	    //    every k steps (looksam.py sam_step + looksam.h:27-59):
556	    //      ‖g‖     = GLOBAL L2 norm over ALL reduced grads (compute_sam_grad_norm_
557	    //                device_side); rho_over_norm = rho/‖g‖
558	    //      p'      = p + rho_over_norm·g          (perturb in the grad direction;
559	    //                backup = p.clone() for the exact restore — fp32 add is not
560	    //                bit-reversible, so we MUST save, not subtract back)
561	    //      g_sam   = ∇L(p')                       (a FULL SECOND in-kernel fwd+bwd
562	    //                + deterministic grad assembly at the perturbed weights, written
563	    //                to the SEPARATE `sam_grad` buffer so `grad` (the first grad the
564	    //                apply tail blends from) is untouched)
565	    //      sam_dir = g_sam − g                    (cached in the PERSISTENT `extra`
566	    //                state slice == st.sam_dir; reused verbatim on the k−1 intervening
567	    //                steps where looksam_sam==0, so NO 2nd pass runs then)
568	    //      restore p = backup
569	    //    The apply tail (P3, apply_optimizer<LookSAM>) then blends g_adj=(1−α)g+α·
570	    //    sam_dir and runs AdamW — UNCHANGED. DETERMINISM: the ‖g‖ reduction is the
571	    //    IDENTICAL deterministic ascending-CTA shape as GrokAdamW's P2.5 (fixed
572	    //    contiguous per-CTA range → per-CTA partial → CTA0 ascending sum), and the
573	    //    2nd fwd+bwd+assembly reuses the SAME A/A/A-clean machinery as the first pass
574	    //    (fixed tile ownership, ascending-k reductions), so the whole phase is
575	    //    deterministic BY CONSTRUCTION. Guarded so every other opt's path is
576	    //    byte-identical (no extra barrier / work). On a NON-SAM step (looksam_sam==0)
577	    //    this whole block is skipped — st.sam_dir already holds the cached direction.
578	    //
579	    //    SuperGrok11/15 SHARE this exact SAM 2nd-backward machinery (INTEGRATION-
580	    //    OPTSTAGES §4/§5): the perturb→2nd in-kernel fwd+bwd→restore pipeline is
581	    //    IDENTICAL; only the elementwise WRITE in step (d) differs — LookSAM writes
582	    //    st.sam_dir[i] = g_sam − g, SG11/15 write st.sharpness[i] = (g_sam − g)²

57	//  §1.3  SM-pinning: read the streaming-multiprocessor id via %smid.
58	//
59	//  The host launches exactly gridDim.x == #SMs CTAs (one persistent CTA per
60	//  SM) and uses sm_id() inside the kernel to index that SM's resident slice
61	//  of optimizer state, so the slice stays warm in this SM's L2 partition for
62	//  the whole step. On pre-sm_90 the asm is still valid (%smid exists since
63	//  sm_20); the guard only exists to keep a host-compile of this header clean.

65	__device__ __forceinline__ unsigned sm_id() {
66	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__)
67	    unsigned id;
68	    asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %%smid;" : "=r"(id));

70	#else
71	    return 0u;
72	#endif

75	// =========================================================================
76	//  §1.1 / §1.2  TaskQueue — global work counter + work-stealing.
77	//
78	//  One int in global memory (`g_next_task`, zero-initialized by the host).
79	//  Every CTA runs:
80	//      for (int t = q.next(); t < n_tasks; t = q.next()) process(t);
81	//  next() does `atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1)` — a CTA that drains its tensor
82	//  early just grabs the next index, so faster SMs steal work from the queue
83	//  with no static load-balancing (§1.2). The atomic is the ONLY synchronizer;
84	//  task bodies are independent (one parameter tensor each), so no fence is
85	//  needed on the *pull* — the fence belongs at the grid barrier between the
86	//  forward / backward / optimizer phases (§1.4), not on the per-task pull.
87	//
88	//  By convention ONE thread per CTA (the elected leader) pulls a task and
89	//  broadcasts it to the block via shared memory; `next_block()` packages that.
90	// =========================================================================
91	struct TaskQueue {
92	    int* g_next_task;   // global counter (host memset to 0 before launch)
93	    int  n_tasks;       // total parameter tensors to process this phase
94	
95	    __device__ __forceinline__ explicit TaskQueue(int* counter, int total)
96	        : g_next_task(counter), n_tasks(total) {}
97	
98	    // Per-thread atomic pull (used when every thread independently claims work,
99	    // e.g. a warp-granular schedule). Returns a task index that may be >=
100	    // n_tasks (caller bounds-checks).
101	    __device__ __forceinline__ int next() {
102	        return atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1);
103	    }
104	
105	    // Per-CTA pull: the leader thread does the single atomicAdd and broadcasts
106	    // the claimed index to the whole block through `smem_slot`. All threads in
107	    // the block then cooperate on that one tensor. Returns the claimed index.
108	    __device__ __forceinline__ int next_block(int* smem_slot) {
109	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
110	            *smem_slot = atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1);
111	        }
112	        __syncthreads();
113	        int t = *smem_slot;
114	        __syncthreads();   // ensure every thread read before slot is reused
115	        return t;
116	    }
117	};

119	// =========================================================================
120	//  §1.4  GridBarrier — hand-built, reusable, sense-reversing grid barrier.
121	//
122	//  State (all in global memory, host-zero-initialized):
123	//    arrived    — count of CTAs that have reached the current barrier
124	//    generation — flips/advances each time the barrier is crossed (the "sense"
125	//                 a late CTA waits on so an early CTA can't lap it)
126	//
127	//  The classic correctness hazard with a counter barrier is *reuse*: if you
128	//  just reset `arrived` to 0, a fast CTA can enter the NEXT barrier and
129	//  increment the counter before a slow CTA has observed the release of the
130	//  PREVIOUS one. The sense-reversing generation fixes this: each CTA samples
131	//  the generation on entry, then waits until the generation has ADVANCED
132	//  (the last arriver advances it), never touching `arrived` for reset on the
133	//  consumer side. The last CTA to arrive resets `arrived` to 0 and bumps the
134	//  generation in one release; everyone else spins on the generation.
135	//
136	//  Fences (§1.14):
137	//    * The releasing writes a CTA makes BEFORE the barrier (its phase output)
138	//      must be visible to peers AFTER the barrier. We publish arrival with a
139	//      __threadfence() (device-scope release) before the atomicAdd, and the
140	//      waiters do an acquire by reading the generation with volatile semantics
141	//      and a __threadfence() after the wait completes. Exactly two fences per
142	//      CTA per barrier — the minimum for a correct release/acquire pair.
143	//
144	//  Only thread 0 of each CTA participates in the cross-CTA handshake; the rest
145	//  of the block is gated by a __syncthreads() so the whole CTA leaves together.
146	// =========================================================================
147	struct GridBarrier {
148	    unsigned* g_arrived;      // CTAs arrived at current phase
149	    unsigned* g_generation;   // sense-reversing generation counter
150	    unsigned  n_ctas;         // gridDim.x (CTAs that must arrive)
151	
152	    __device__ __forceinline__ GridBarrier(unsigned* arrived,
153	                                            unsigned* generation,
154	                                            unsigned grid_ctas)
155	        : g_arrived(arrived), g_generation(generation), n_ctas(grid_ctas) {}
156	
157	    __device__ __forceinline__ void sync() const {
158	        // The block must fully reach the barrier before its leader publishes.
159	        __syncthreads();
160	
161	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
162	            // Sample the sense we are waiting to leave.
163	            unsigned my_gen =
164	                *reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation);
165	
166	            // §1.14 RELEASE: make this CTA's phase writes visible device-wide
167	            // BEFORE we announce arrival, so a peer that observes our arrival
168	            // (and crosses) also observes our outputs.
169	            __threadfence();
170	
171	            // Atomically join the arrival count. The CTA whose add completes
172	            // the set (== n_ctas) is the "last arriver".
173	            unsigned prev = atomicAdd(g_arrived, 1u);
174	            if (prev + 1u == n_ctas) {
175	                // Last arriver: clear the count for the NEXT phase, then bump
176	                // the generation. Order matters — reset arrived to 0 first,
177	                // then a release-store of the advanced generation so a CTA that
178	                // sees the new generation also sees arrived==0 when it next
179	                // enters. atomicExch gives the store device-scope visibility.
180	                atomicExch(g_arrived, 0u);
181	                __threadfence();
182	                atomicAdd(g_generation, 1u);
183	            } else {
184	                // Not last: spin until the generation advances past our sample.
185	                // §1.14b BACKOFF: a tight volatile-read spin hammers the L2 /
186	                // memory subsystem with the generation poll and steals issue
187	                // slots from arriving CTAs. __nanosleep parks the spinning warp
188	                // for an exponentially-growing nap (capped) so the poll rate
189	                // drops and the memory subsystem is left to the laggard CTAs.
190	                // Behavior-preserving: still exits the instant the generation
191	                // advances; only the *poll cadence* changes (sm_70+; on older
192	                // arches the asm is a no-op fallback).
193	                unsigned backoff = 32u;
194	                while (*reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation)
195	                       == my_gen) {
196	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 700)
197	                    __nanosleep(backoff);
198	                    backoff = (backoff < 1024u) ? (backoff << 1) : 1024u;
199	#endif
200	                }
201	            }
202	
203	            // §1.14 ACQUIRE: after observing the generation advance, fence so
204	            // the peers' phase writes (released above) are visible to us.
205	            __threadfence();
206	        }
207	
208	        // Release the rest of the block once the leader has crossed.
209	        __syncthreads();
210	    }

212	    // #4 — barrier with a FUSED task-counter reset. The L3 phase loop used to do
213	    //   fwd → sync → reset_counter → sync → bwd → sync → reset_counter → sync
214	    // (4 grid barriers + 2 standalone in-kernel counter resets). The reset is
215	    // folded into THIS barrier's last-arriver critical section: the last CTA
216	    // zeroes `*reset_counter` BEFORE the release-store that advances the
217	    // generation, so any CTA that later observes the new generation (and thus
218	    // crosses) is guaranteed to see the counter == 0 for the next phase. That
219	    // removes the two standalone resets AND their two barriers — 4 → 2 grid
220	    // barriers per L3 step — with identical phase ordering/visibility. Pass the
221	    // task-queue counter (ctx.g_next_task) as `reset_counter`.
222	    __device__ __forceinline__ void sync_reset(int* reset_counter) const {
223	        __syncthreads();
224	
225	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
226	            unsigned my_gen =
227	                *reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation);
228	            __threadfence();   // §1.14 RELEASE: publish phase writes before arrival.
229	            unsigned prev = atomicAdd(g_arrived, 1u);
230	            if (prev + 1u == n_ctas) {
231	                // Last arriver: clear arrival count AND reset the task counter
232	                // for the next phase, then a release-store of the advanced
233	                // generation. Ordering: both resets, then __threadfence(), then
234	                // the generation bump — so observers of the new gen see both
235	                // arrived==0 and reset_counter==0.
236	                atomicExch(g_arrived, 0u);
237	                atomicExch(reinterpret_cast<unsigned*>(reset_counter), 0u);
238	                __threadfence();
239	                atomicAdd(g_generation, 1u);
240	            } else {
241	                unsigned backoff = 32u;
242	                while (*reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation)
243	                       == my_gen) {
244	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 700)
245	                    __nanosleep(backoff);
246	                    backoff = (backoff < 1024u) ? (backoff << 1) : 1024u;
247	#endif
248	                }
249	            }
250	            __threadfence();   // §1.14 ACQUIRE.
251	        }
252	
253	        __syncthreads();
254	    }
255	};
256	
257	// =========================================================================
258	//  PersistentContext — the bundle of global scratch a generated L3 megakernel
259	//  needs. The host allocates these (all zero-initialized) and passes their
260	//  device pointers to the kernel. Grouping them keeps the generated kernel
261	//  signatures uniform across all 99 cells.
262	// =========================================================================
263	struct PersistentContext {
264	    int*      g_next_task;     // §1.1 TaskQueue counter
265	    unsigned* g_arrived;       // §1.4 GridBarrier arrival count
266	    unsigned* g_generation;    // §1.4 GridBarrier generation
267	    int       n_tasks;         // parameter tensors this step
268	    unsigned  n_ctas;          // persistent CTAs (== #SMs, one per SM, §1.3)
269	
270	    __device__ __forceinline__ TaskQueue queue() const {
271	        return TaskQueue(g_next_task, n_tasks);
272	    }
273	    __device__ __forceinline__ GridBarrier barrier() const {
274	        return GridBarrier(g_arrived, g_generation, n_ctas);
275	    }
276	};

222	//  K=16 bf16) MUST be in the CUTLASS Major-K INTERLEAVE layout (wgmma.cuh):
223	//      idx(mn,k) = (k/8)*(MN*8) + mn*8 + (k%8)
224	//  This helper writes ONE such MN x 16 tile, pulling element (mn, k) from a
225	//  caller-provided accessor `src(mn, kbase + k)`. Routing the source axis
226	//  through the accessor is what lets the SAME wgmma issue (TransA=0/TransB=0,
227	//  the substrate-validated orientation) serve fwd / dX / dW: the staging loop
228	//  transposes physically; the engine never leaves the gated path.
229	//
230	//  Cooperative over `nthreads` threads starting at thread `t0` (a warpgroup).
231	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
232	template <int MN, typename Src>
233	__device__ __forceinline__ void stage_kmajor_tile(
234	        __nv_bfloat16* smem_tile, int kbase, Src src, int t0, int nthreads) {
235	    // MN*16 elements, each thread strides.
236	    #pragma unroll 1
237	    for (int i = t0; i < MN * wgs::kWgmmaAtomK; i += nthreads) {
238	        const int mn = i / wgs::kWgmmaAtomK;
239	        const int k  = i % wgs::kWgmmaAtomK;
240	        const int dst = (k >> 3) * (MN * 8) + mn * 8 + (k & 7);
241	        smem_tile[dst] = src(mn, kbase + k);
242	    }
243	}

245	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
246	//  Unpipelined single-CTA batch GEMM: D[M,N] = Σ_k A[m,k]·B[n,k], bf16 operands
247	//  (accessor-sourced + Major-K staged), fp32 accumulator, ascending-k. M is
248	//  kTileM (kAtomsM stacked m64 atoms — the substrate's unexercised TILE_M
249	//  stacking, gated here). N is a compile-time wgmma atom width. K=k_steps*16.
250	//
251	//  The consumer warpgroup (the FULL CTA's 256 threads act as producer+consumer
252	//  here in the SIMPLE unpipelined form: all 256 stage, then warpgroup 0's 128
253	//  threads — actually wgmma is warpgroup-scoped (.aligned, 128 threads). We use
254	//  ONE warpgroup (threads 0..127) for the MMA; staging uses all 256 threads.
255	//
256	//  smem: one A tile (64x16) + one B tile (Nx16) per stacked atom row, reused
257	//  across k-steps (unpipelined: stage k, mma k, repeat). Two buffers (A,B) of
258	//  the largest atom. Accumulators live in registers (kAtomsM fragments).
259	//
260	//  ACC OUTPUT: written via accessor `out(m_global, n_local, value)` so the
261	//  caller routes the fp32 result (the fragment decode gives (row,col) within the
262	//  64xN atom; the caller adds the atom's M-base).
263	//
264	//  GENERALITY (the M and N must be caller-parameterized, NOT hardwired to the
265	//  token tile — a dW GEMM has M = Nout in {99,128,384,512} and the fwd GEMMs
266	//  have N in {128,384,512}). This helper computes ONE M-block of `m_atoms`
267	//  stacked m64 atoms (rows [mbase0, mbase0 + m_atoms*64)) for ONE N-tile of the
268	//  compile-time atom width N. The CALLER loops M-atom-blocks × N-tiles to cover
269	//  arbitrary (M, N). MaxAtomsM bounds the register accumulator array
270	//  (compile-time); only `m_atoms` (<= MaxAtomsM) atoms are issued at runtime.
271	//  `n_real <= N` lets the caller mark the valid column count for a ragged N-tile
272	//  (e.g. head V=99 in a N=128 tile) so the epilogue suppresses pad columns; the
273	//  wgmma still runs the full N (pad operands are zero so pad outputs are inert).
274	//
275	//  Determinism: ascending-k, one CTA owns the tile end-to-end, no atomics.
276	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
277	template <int N, int MaxAtomsM, typename SrcA, typename SrcB, typename Out>
278	__device__ void tc_gemm_block_unpipelined(
279	        int mbase0, int m_atoms, int n_real, int k_steps,
280	        SrcA srcA, SrcB srcB, Out out,
281	        __nv_bfloat16* smemA, __nv_bfloat16* smemB) {
282	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
283	    const int tid = threadIdx.x;
284	    const int nthreads = blockDim.x;            // 256
285	    const bool in_wg0 = (tid < 128);
286	    const int tid_wg = tid & 127;
287	
288	    // One fp32 accumulator fragment per stacked m64 atom (compile-time bound).
289	    wgs::WgmmaAccum<N> acc[MaxAtomsM];
290	    constexpr int S = kDecTcStages;
291	
292	    // Stage tile `k` of atom `mbase` into ring slot `k % S` (smem{A,B} are ring bases).
293	    auto stage_k = [&] (int mbase, int k) {
294	        const int sl = k % S;
295	        stage_kmajor_tile<wgs::kWgmmaAtomM>(
296	            smemA + (int64_t)sl * kDecTcSmemA1, k * wgs::kWgmmaAtomK,
297	            [&] (int mn, int kk) { return srcA(mbase + mn, kk); }, tid, nthreads);
298	        stage_kmajor_tile<N>(
299	            smemB + (int64_t)sl * kDecTcSmemB1, k * wgs::kWgmmaAtomK,
300	            [&] (int mn, int kk) { return srcB(mn, kk); }, tid, nthreads);
301	    };
302	    auto issue_k = [&] (int a, int k) {
303	        const int sl = k % S;
304	        wgs::SmemDesc dA = wgs::make_desc_A_kmajor<wgs::kWgmmaAtomM, wgs::kSwizzleNone>(
305	            smemA + (int64_t)sl * kDecTcSmemA1);
306	        wgs::SmemDesc dB = wgs::make_desc_B_kmajor<N, wgs::kSwizzleNone>(
307	            smemB + (int64_t)sl * kDecTcSmemB1);
308	        if (k == 0) wgs::wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/0, 0, 0>(acc[a], dA, dB);
309	        else        wgs::wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/1, 0, 0>(acc[a], dA, dB);
310	    };
311	
312	    // For each stacked atom (M-base = mbase0 + a*64), run the full k-chain.
313	    #pragma unroll 1
314	    for (int a = 0; a < m_atoms; ++a) {
315	        const int mbase = mbase0 + a * wgs::kWgmmaAtomM;
316	        // Prologue: stage tile 0; make visible; fence.
317	        stage_k(mbase, 0);
318	        __syncthreads();
319	        if (in_wg0) wgs::wgmma_fence();
320	        // Steady state (S=2 single-in-flight double-buffer): issue wgmma(k) on the
321	        // already-staged slot k&1 (async), THEN stage tile k+1 into the OTHER slot
322	        // (its HBM loads overlap the MMA), THEN wait_group<0> + sync (wgmma(k) done
323	        // reading slot k&1; stage(k+1) visible; slot k&1 reuse-safe). S=1 collapses
324	        // to the validated serial path (stage k+1 into the single slot AFTER wait).
325	        #pragma unroll 1
326	        for (int k = 0; k < k_steps; ++k) {
327	            if (in_wg0) { issue_k(a, k); wgs::wgmma_commit_group(); }
328	            if (S > 1) {
329	                if (k + 1 < k_steps) stage_k(mbase, k + 1);
330	                if (in_wg0) wgs::wgmma_wait_group<0>();
331	                __syncthreads();
332	            } else {
333	                if (in_wg0) wgs::wgmma_wait_group<0>();
334	                __syncthreads();
335	                if (k + 1 < k_steps) { stage_k(mbase, k + 1); __syncthreads(); }
336	            }
337	        }
338	        // Epilogue: warpgroup 0 owns the fp32 fragment; decode + emit (real cols).
339	        if (in_wg0) {
340	            #pragma unroll
341	            for (int i = 0; i < wgs::WgmmaAccum<N>::kRegs; ++i) {
342	                int row, col;
343	                wgs::wgmma_frag_decode(tid_wg, i, N, row, col);
344	                if (col < n_real) out(mbase + row, col, acc[a].c[i]);
345	            }
346	        }
347	        __syncthreads();
348	    }
349	#else
350	    (void)mbase0; (void)m_atoms; (void)n_real; (void)k_steps;
351	    (void)srcA; (void)srcB; (void)out; (void)smemA; (void)smemB;
352	#endif
353	}

355	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
356	//  THIN ORIENTATION WRAPPERS over tc_gemm_block_unpipelined. These reproduce
357	//  the THREE accessor patterns the engine is silicon-validated on
358	//  (decoder_tc_selftest.cu / test_decoder_tc.py 13/13): fwd (Y=X·Wᵀ, no
359	//  transpose), dX (dX=dY·W, W transposed-staged), dW (dW=dYᵀ·X, BOTH
360	//  transposed-staged, K=T). The driver calls THESE — it never re-derives the
361	//  staging (the no-suppression / reuse-the-validated-unit discipline).
362	//
363	//  All operands are HBM bf16 row-major. The caller passes one A(64×16) + one
364	//  B(Nmax×16) smem staging pair (the engine reuses them across k-steps). N is
365	//  the compile-time wgmma atom width (128 for in/out/ff dX-N=d; the fwd loops
366	//  N-tiles internally). Accumulation is fp32; output written via the accessor.
367	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
368	
369	// (fwd) Y[M,Nout] = X[M,Kin] @ W[Nout,Kin]ᵀ.  Tiles N over [0,Nout) in width-N
370	// atoms (Nout∈{d=128, 3d=384, dff=512}). M = kTileM (kAtomsM stacked atoms).
371	// Y is written row-major [M, Nout] at base `Yout` with row stride Nout.
372	// NOTE on weights: the params blob is fp32; the wgmma engine needs bf16 B
373	// operands. We convert ON READ in the accessor (`__float2bfloat16(W[...])`) —
374	// deterministic, so every read yields the same bf16 (determinism-safe), and it
375	// needs NO bf16 weight buffer or cross-CTA conversion phase. Cost: weight bytes
376	// read as fp32 (2×) in fwd/dX — a perf-phase optimization, not a correctness gate.
377	template <int N>
378	__device__ __forceinline__ void dectc_gemm_fwd(
379	        const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ X, const float* __restrict__ W,
380	        __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ Yout, int Kin, int Nout,
381	        __nv_bfloat16* sA, __nv_bfloat16* sB) {
382	    const int k_steps = Kin / wgs::kWgmmaAtomK;
383	    for (int n0 = 0; n0 < Nout; n0 += N) {
384	        const int n_real = (Nout - n0) < N ? (Nout - n0) : N;
385	        auto srcA = [&] (int m, int k) -> __nv_bfloat16 { return X[(int64_t)m * Kin + k]; };
386	        auto srcB = [&] (int n, int k) -> __nv_bfloat16 {
387	            int nn = n0 + n; return nn < Nout ? __float2bfloat16(W[(int64_t)nn * Kin + k]) : __float2bfloat16(0.f); };
388	        auto out  = [&] (int m, int n, float v) {
389	            Yout[(int64_t)m * Nout + n0 + n] = __float2bfloat16(v); };
390	        tc_gemm_block_unpipelined<N, /*MaxAtomsM=*/kAtomsM>(
391	            0, kAtomsM, n_real, k_steps, srcA, srcB, out, sA, sB);
392	    }
393	}

395	// Same as dectc_gemm_fwd but emits the fp32 result (no bf16 round) — for the
396	// few fwd outputs consumed by fp32 elementwise stages directly. Writes [M,Nout]
397	// fp32 at `Yf32`.
398	template <int N>
399	__device__ __forceinline__ void dectc_gemm_fwd_f32(
400	        const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ X, const float* __restrict__ W,
401	        float* __restrict__ Yf32, int Kin, int Nout,
402	        __nv_bfloat16* sA, __nv_bfloat16* sB) {
403	    const int k_steps = Kin / wgs::kWgmmaAtomK;
404	    for (int n0 = 0; n0 < Nout; n0 += N) {
405	        const int n_real = (Nout - n0) < N ? (Nout - n0) : N;
406	        auto srcA = [&] (int m, int k) -> __nv_bfloat16 { return X[(int64_t)m * Kin + k]; };
407	        auto srcB = [&] (int n, int k) -> __nv_bfloat16 {
408	            int nn = n0 + n; return nn < Nout ? __float2bfloat16(W[(int64_t)nn * Kin + k]) : __float2bfloat16(0.f); };
409	        auto out  = [&] (int m, int n, float v) { Yf32[(int64_t)m * Nout + n0 + n] = v; };
410	        tc_gemm_block_unpipelined<N, /*MaxAtomsM=*/kAtomsM>(
411	            0, kAtomsM, n_real, k_steps, srcA, srcB, out, sA, sB);
412	    }
413	}
414	
415	// (dX) dX[M,Kin] = dY[M,Nout] @ W[Nout,Kin].  N(wgmma) = Kin (the in_dim, tiled
416	// by width N). K = Nout (the contracted out_dim). W is staged transposed:
417	// srcB(n=kin, k=out) = W[out·Kin + kin] (fp32 → bf16 on read). Writes fp32 dX
418	// [M,Kin] (LN/elementwise bwd consume it fp32).
419	template <int N>
420	__device__ __forceinline__ void dectc_gemm_dx_f32(
421	        const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ dY, const float* __restrict__ W,
422	        float* __restrict__ dXf32, int Kin, int Nout,
423	        __nv_bfloat16* sA, __nv_bfloat16* sB) {
424	    const int k_steps = Nout / wgs::kWgmmaAtomK;
425	    for (int n0 = 0; n0 < Kin; n0 += N) {
426	        const int n_real = (Kin - n0) < N ? (Kin - n0) : N;
427	        auto srcA = [&] (int m, int k) -> __nv_bfloat16 { return dY[(int64_t)m * Nout + k]; };
428	        // B[n=kin, k=out] = W[out, kin]  (transposed read; fp32 → bf16).
429	        auto srcB = [&] (int n, int k) -> __nv_bfloat16 {
430	            int nn = n0 + n; return nn < Kin ? __float2bfloat16(W[(int64_t)k * Kin + nn]) : __float2bfloat16(0.f); };
431	        auto out  = [&] (int m, int n, float v) { dXf32[(int64_t)m * Kin + n0 + n] = v; };
432	        tc_gemm_block_unpipelined<N, /*MaxAtomsM=*/kAtomsM>(
433	            0, kAtomsM, n_real, k_steps, srcA, srcB, out, sA, sB);
434	    }
435	}

437	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
438	//  Per-CTA TILE SCRATCH (HBM). One tile's forward intermediates the backward
439	//  reads, reused across the tiles a CTA grid-strides over (a CTA finishes a
440	//  tile's fwd+bwd before the next tile, so one slab per CTA suffices). Sized
441	//  for kTileM rows. The X-inputs / dY-adjoints that OTHER CTAs read in P2's dW
442	//  do NOT live here — they live in the full-T DecActs (cross-CTA). This holds
443	//  only the within-tile fwd state + the running adjoint so the backward needs
444	//  NO recompute.
445	//
446	//  DEDICATED, NON-ALIASED buffers (the TC test sizes its own workspace; HBM is
447	//  NOT scarce, so hand-managed aliasing — the stride/alias bug class that bit
448	//  the scalar path at model_stages_decoder.cuh:619-625, which the CPU mirror
449	//  does NOT cover for tile-batched reuse — is avoided entirely). Each fp32
450	//  intermediate gets its own slot.
451	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
452	
453	// nSamp samples per tile, H*S*S attention entries each; V logits each.
454	constexpr int kNSampPerTile  = kTileM / dec::kSeq;
455	constexpr int kAttnPerTile   = kNSampPerTile * dec::kHeads * dec::kSeq * dec::kSeq;
456	constexpr int kLogitsPerTile = kNSampPerTile * dec::kVocab;
457	
458	// CRITICAL: the forward runs ALL layers, THEN the backward runs ALL layers (NOT
459	// interleaved per-layer). So every forward intermediate the backward reads PER
460	// LAYER must be stored PER LAYER — a single-buffered cache holds only the LAST
461	// layer's values and the earlier layers' backward reads garbage (the "forward
462	// exact, layer-0 grads wrong, error compounds backward" bug). qkv / ff0pre /
463	// attn / n1·n2 LN caches are therefore [kLayers]-indexed. fnx/fni (final norm,
464	// one instance) + the transient dh/x1/finalin/logits/work/work2/dsc stay single.
465	struct DecTileScratch {
466	    __nv_bfloat16* qkv[dec::kLayers];     // [kTileM, 3d]  per layer
467	    __nv_bfloat16* ff0pre[dec::kLayers];  // [kTileM, dff] per layer
468	    float* attn[dec::kLayers];            // [kAttnPerTile] per layer
469	    float* n1x[dec::kLayers]; float* n1i[dec::kLayers];
470	    float* n2x[dec::kLayers]; float* n2i[dec::kLayers];
471	    float* dsc;             // [kAttnPerTile] attention dscores (transient, bwd-only)
472	    float* fnx; float* fni; // final-norm LN caches (single)
473	    float* dh;              // [kTileM, d]    running adjoint wrt block output
474	    float* x1;              // [kTileM, d]    n1 output (fp32, residual base for r2)
475	    float* finalin;         // [kTileM, d]    last-layer n2 output (fp32, head input)
476	    float* logits;          // [kLogitsPerTile] per-sample last-pos logits (fp32)
477	    float* work;            // [kTileM, dff]  GEMM output / general fp32 scratch
478	    float* work2;           // [kTileM, dff]  second fp32 scratch (bwd dx1/dqkv)
479	};
480	
481	// Bytes one CTA's scratch occupies (for host sizing of the workspace tail).
482	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t dec_tile_scratch_bf16_count() {
483	    // (qkv + ff0pre) per layer.
484	    return (int64_t)dec::kLayers * ((int64_t)kTileM * 3 * dec::kD + (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kDff);
485	}
486	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t dec_tile_scratch_f32_count() {
487	    return (int64_t)dec::kLayers * (                     // per-layer:
488	             (int64_t)kAttnPerTile                       //   attn
489	           + 2 * ((int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD + kTileM))    //   n1+n2 xhat+inv
490	         + (int64_t)kAttnPerTile                          // dsc (single)
491	         + ((int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD + kTileM)           // fn xhat+inv (single)
492	         + (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD                      // dh
493	         + (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD                      // x1
494	         + (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD                      // finalin
495	         + (int64_t)kLogitsPerTile                        // logits
496	         + 2 * (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kDff;               // work + work2
497	}
498	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t dec_tile_scratch_total_f32() {
499	    return (dec_tile_scratch_bf16_count() + 1) / 2 + dec_tile_scratch_f32_count();
500	}
501	
502	__device__ __forceinline__ DecTileScratch dec_tile_scratch_bind(float* slab) {
503	    DecTileScratch s;
504	    __nv_bfloat16* b = reinterpret_cast<__nv_bfloat16*>(slab);
505	    int64_t bo = 0;
506	    for (int li = 0; li < dec::kLayers; ++li) { s.qkv[li]    = b + bo; bo += (int64_t)kTileM * 3 * dec::kD; }
507	    for (int li = 0; li < dec::kLayers; ++li) { s.ff0pre[li] = b + bo; bo += (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kDff; }
508	    float* f = slab + (dec_tile_scratch_bf16_count() + 1) / 2;
509	    int64_t fo = 0;
510	    for (int li = 0; li < dec::kLayers; ++li) { s.attn[li] = f + fo; fo += kAttnPerTile; }
511	    for (int li = 0; li < dec::kLayers; ++li) { s.n1x[li] = f + fo; fo += (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD; s.n1i[li] = f + fo; fo += kTileM; }
512	    for (int li = 0; li < dec::kLayers; ++li) { s.n2x[li] = f + fo; fo += (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD; s.n2i[li] = f + fo; fo += kTileM; }
513	    s.dsc  = f + fo; fo += kAttnPerTile;
514	    s.fnx  = f + fo; fo += (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD;
515	    s.fni  = f + fo; fo += kTileM;
516	    s.dh   = f + fo; fo += (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD;
517	    s.x1   = f + fo; fo += (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD;
518	    s.finalin = f + fo; fo += (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kD;
519	    s.logits  = f + fo; fo += kLogitsPerTile;
520	    s.work    = f + fo; fo += (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kDff;
521	    s.work2   = f + fo; fo += (int64_t)kTileM * dec::kDff;
522	    return s;
523	}
